Particulate Nature 
of Matter 
7

water?
 
z Why does water take the shape of folded hands but lose that 
shape when released?
 
z We cannot see air, so how does it add weight to an inflated 
balloon?
 
z Is the air we breathe today the same that 
existed thousands of years ago?
 
z Share your questions 
 
 ?
Probe and ponder

You learnt that the chalk does not change into a new substance on grinding.

Let us imagine that this process of grinding continues.

correctItems.text: Eventually, we would reach a stage where the chalk particles cannot be broken down any further.
The tiny units obtained at this stage are the basic building blocks that the chalk was made up of.
This means that one whole piece of chalk was made up of a large number of smaller units.
A constituent particle is the basic unit that makes up a larger piece of a substance or material.
